$comment: P69 fold 3c (lane `xa`), D-LK-ELF-READER-KEEPS-EVERY-SECTION-GROUP-AND-DISCARDS-NONE, part (c). Two ELF objects each carry COMDAT group `h`, whose member `.text.h` DEFINES `h` -- global, hidden and STRONG, what a C++ compiler writes for an inline function of a hidden class -- and each calls `h` by name from a function of its own. Two strong definitions of one name: no rule of name resolution settles them, and the format never asks one to, because its linkers keep the FIRST unit's group of a signature and discard every later one with all it holds before any name is resolved. GNU ld 2.42 and ld.lld 18.1.3 link the pair in either order (MEASURED 2026-10-20: 77 with unit A first, 99 with unit B first); DSS refused both orders, two strong definitions of `h` across units, until P69 fold 3c discarded the later group. Unit A first: both callers answer 7, exit 77. The other order is `elf_group_hidden_pair_other_order`.
